principles: tamper.mjs READS the frozen protocol.json; it never re-derives or rewrites fingerprints (conformance to the M0 freeze is the whole point).
fingerprintMatch over the explicit frozen domain (flags + numeric predicates) is the mechanical H2 adjudication (no textual reason).
Reuse M0 lib/instrument.mjs; do not duplicate verify/refresh/fingerprint logic.
All mutations on mkdtemp copies; identity-keyed canonical verdict ledger.
Fail loudly: any live-vs-frozen mismatch exits nonzero (H2 evidence must be un-gameable).
drivers: The frozen protocol.json is the M0 contract; M1 proves conformance, not re-discovery.
The verifier has no reason field, forcing fingerprint-based adjudication.
tamper-verdicts.jsonl must be reproducible + machine-adjudicable by the M4 analyzer.

options.name: read-frozen-protocol-assert-conformance
pros: Catches instrument drift vs the freeze
Verdict ledger is the reproducible H2 evidence
cons: Requires the class mutation definitions to match M0 exactly

options.name: recompute-fingerprints-in-tamper
cons: Makes the M0 freeze meaningless — no conformance check; H2 becomes unfalsifiable

rationale: M1 must prove the instrument still conforms to the frozen fingerprints (that is H2 evidence). Recomputing fingerprints inside tamper.mjs would defeat the freeze. Reusing the M0 mutations + lib keeps it deterministic and drift-detecting.

preMortem.scenario: Fingerprint mismatch from a benign representation diff
preMortem.trigger: live verify returns a numeric rate as 0.9999999 vs frozen 1 due to float
preMortem.mitigation: compare numeric predicates via the frozen op/value (exact/threshold), not raw float equality

preMortem.trigger: volatile fields (elapsedMs/rss/absolute paths) written into tamper-verdicts.jsonl
preMortem.mitigation: exclude volatile fields from the identity/verdict content; keep only the frozen-domain values + fingerprintMatch

preMortem.scenario: Harness mutations drift from the M0 class definitions
preMortem.trigger: tamper.mjs re-implements a mutation differently than viability-check.mjs
preMortem.consequence: a class produces a different fingerprint and spuriously mismatches
preMortem.mitigation: share the mutation/class definitions with M0 (import or replicate verbatim) and let the selfcheck negative test catch drift
